name: CentralReach
subcategory: ABA practice management and clinical billing
tagline: Practice management, clinical data collection, scheduling and insurance billing for ABA and autism care providers.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. CentralReach sells by quote, typically per-user with implementation fees, and does not publish rates.

verdictSummary: The visible surface of CentralReach looks like a CRUD app: clients, staff, appointments, session notes, trial data, invoices. The actual product is the plumbing behind that: electronic claims to specific payers, authorization and unit tracking, payer-specific rules, HIPAA obligations with a signed BAA, audit trails that survive an insurance audit, and credential tracking for RBTs and BCBAs. An agent can absolutely build you a local data collection and session log tool in a session, and that piece is genuinely fine. What it cannot build is a clearinghouse relationship, a payer rules engine, or the legal posture that lets a clinic bill Medicaid without getting clawed back. If you are a solo practitioner doing cash pay with a handful of clients, the DIY version is real; if a single dollar of your revenue comes from insurance, do not do this.
coreLoopDIY: A local single-clinician app for clients, programs and targets, trial-by-trial session data collection with graphs, session notes and a billable time log with CSV export.
requirements: local machine you control, ideally disk-encrypted
a tablet-sized browser if you want to take data during sessions
your own legal review before any real client data goes in
whatYouLose: Electronic claim submission, scrubbing and remittance handling through a clearinghouse
Insurance authorization and unit tracking, so you find out about overbilling the hard way
HIPAA posture: signed BAA, access logs, audit-ready record retention
Staff scheduling with credential and supervision-ratio checks, plus payroll export
Offline mobile data collection that keeps working in a client's living room with bad wifi
moatNotes: Billing ABA to insurance is a rules problem, not a UI problem, and the rules change per payer per state.
whyPeopleStillPay: Clinics do not pay CentralReach for the forms, they pay it to get reimbursed. Revenue cycle management for ABA is a specialised nightmare of authorizations, units, CPT codes, supervision ratios and payer quirks, and a clinic that gets it wrong either loses money quietly or gets audited loudly. Layer on HIPAA, years of historical client records that legally must be retained, and staff who already know where every button is, and switching becomes a board-level decision rather than a tooling preference. A homegrown tool is a plausible replacement for exactly one part of that: taking data during a session.
notes: The data collection screen is a weekend; the reimbursement engine is not. The moat is payer-specific billing rules, clearinghouse integrations and the compliance liability nobody wants to self-host.
prompt:
Build a local-only ABA session data collection app for a single practitioner. Stack: Next.js 14 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, and SQLite via better-sqlite3 with Drizzle ORM. No auth, no cloud, no telemetry, no external API calls. Everything runs on localhost against a file at ./data/app.db.

Data model:
- clients: id, initials or code name, notes, active flag, created date
- programs: id, client id, name, description, target behavior type (skill acquisition or behavior reduction)
- targets: id, program id, name, prompt level list, mastery criterion text, status (baseline, active, mastered, on hold)
- sessions: id, client id, start time, end time, location, billable minutes, note text
- trials: id, session id, target id, timestamp, result (correct, incorrect, prompted, no response), prompt level, optional count value for frequency data

Screens:
1. Client list, create and edit. Show active programs per client.
2. Program and target editor for a client.
3. Session runner: pick a client, start a session timer, then a large-button tablet-friendly grid of active targets. One tap logs a trial. Support discrete trial (correct/incorrect/prompted) and frequency count modes. Undo last trial. Running percent correct per target shown live.
4. Session close: stop timer, auto-fill billable minutes rounded to the nearest 15, free-text note field, save.
5. Progress view per target: line chart of daily percent correct or daily rate, plus a phase-change marker you can add manually. Use a small charting lib, your choice, one only.
6. Export: CSV of trials, CSV of sessions with billable minutes, and a plain text session note per session. Also a button to copy the SQLite file path.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build and do not stub: insurance claims, CPT codes, payer rules, authorization tracking, payroll, multi-user accounts, permissions, e-signatures, HIPAA controls of any kind.

Include a seed script with two fake clients and sample targets, and a README that states in the first paragraph that this stores clinical data unencrypted on the local disk, is not HIPAA compliant, and must not be used for insurance-billed care. Any config goes in .env, and .env is gitignored.
